prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json's condition for skipping JSON pre-parsing only excludes annotations that are exactly `str`. For any other annotation involving `str` — most notably `str | None` (Optional[str]) — it still attempts `json.loads()` on the raw string, which corrupts otherwise-valid string values that happen to parse as JSON (e.g. a plain-text string like "123", "true", or "[a,b]") since they get silently converted to int/bool/list before Pydantic validation ever sees them. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json's condition for skipping JSON pre-parsing only excludes annotations that are exactly `str`. For any other annotation involving `str` — most notably `str | None` (Optional[str]) — it still attempts `json.loads()` on the raw string, which corrupts otherwise-valid string values that happen to parse as JSON (e.g. a plain-text string like "123", "true", or "[a,b]") since they get silently converted to int/bool/list before Pydantic validation ever sees them. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a helper to decide when pre_parse_json should skip parsing for str-containing unions, but they cover different cases. #3056's _is_optional_str unwraps Annotated[...] on each union member before comparing to str, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the common `Optional[Annotated[str, Field(...)]]` pattern. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json compares union args directly against a _SIMPLE_TYPES frozenset without unwrapping Annotated, so an Annotated str member inside a union is not recognized as simple and pre-parsing still runs — leaving that case unfixed. #2032's frozenset approach is also broader than the reported bug: it disables pre-parsing for any union of str/int/float/bool/None (e.g. str | int), whereas #3056 narrowly targets str | None and leaves parsing intact for unions where another type could legitimately be the intended JSON-decoded result.

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a helper to decide when pre_parse_json should skip parsing for str-containing unions, but they cover different cases. #3056's _is_optional_str unwraps Annotated[...] on each union member before comparing to str, so it correctly skips pre-parsing for the common `Optional[Annotated[str, Field(...)]]` pattern. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json compares union args directly against a _SIMPLE_TYPES frozenset without unwrapping Annotated, so an Annotated str member inside a union is not recognized as simple and pre-parsing still runs — leaving that case unfixed. #2032's frozenset approach is also broader than the reported bug: it disables pre-parsing for any union of str/int/float/bool/None (e.g. str | int), whereas #3056 narrowly targets str | None and leaves parsing intact for unions where another type could legitimately be the intended JSON-decoded result.

members.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
members.author: adityuhkapoor
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3056: pre_parse_json's condition for skipping JSON pre-parsing only excludes annotations that are exactly `str`. For any other annotation involving `str` — most notably `str | None` (Optional[str]) — it still attempts `json.loads()` on the raw string, which corrupts otherwise-valid string values that happen to parse as JSON (e.g. a plain-text string like "123", "true", or "[a,b]") since they get silently converted to int/bool/list before Pydantic validation ever sees them.

clusters.pick_reason: #2395 fixes the failure at its exact source (the `attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS` branch in `_handle_reconnection`) by constructing a JSONRPCError/SessionMessage and sending it through the existing `ctx.read_stream_writer`, which matches the message-passing pattern already used elsewhere in this transport for resolving pending calls — a small, localized diff. #3098 addresses the same trigger by instead raising a `StreamableHTTPError` and adds a new recursive `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull that error out of anyio exception groups, which changes the error-propagation contract for callers (catching a raised exception vs. receiving a JSON-RPC error response) and bundles in an unrelated `from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` -> `from __future__ import annotations` cleanup, making it a larger and more invasive change for the same fix.

clusters.pick_reason: Both implement essentially the same quote/escape-aware comma-splitting algorithm in the same file, but #3041 goes further: it first segments the whole header on top-level commas (_split_www_authenticate_segments) and then explicitly scopes extraction to the 'Bearer' scheme via partition on the scheme token (_extract_bearer_auth_params), which directly addresses the 'substring match' failure named in its title (a scheme name embedded in another challenge or value). #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only finds the first space in the entire header and tokenizes everything after it, so it doesn't distinguish between multiple challenges/schemes in a compound WWW-Authenticate header and would remain vulnerable to the same substring-boundary bug #3041 fixes.

members.title: fix(auth): match complete WWW-Authenticate parameters
members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive string/substring operations that broke when auth-param values contained commas inside quoted strings (and could false-match scheme names as substrings). Both PRs replace this with a manual, quote-aware comma tokenizer added to the same function/file (src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py).
